summary.value: The Brussbar is a rare British chicken developed at Cambridge before 1950 by Professor Punnett and his colleague Mr. Pease, pioneers of autosexing breeds. Their goal was a bird with the useful qualities of the Light Sussex whose chicks could be sorted into males and females by color at hatch. They began by crossing Brown Sussex with Barred Rocks, then added productive Light Sussex lines. The breed was standardized in Britain in 1952. Adults have crele plumage, a barred mix of copper and gold. A silver form once existed, but only the gold survives. Autosexing breeders rated the Brussbar among their best dual purpose birds for eggs and meat, yet it never gained a real following and barely made it through the 1960s. Interest is growing again, though only one known pure flock remains, so it suits dedicated rare breed keepers.
